package_info.package_versions: various versions distributed during the SmoothOperator campaign (March 2023)
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CXDesktopApp installer was trojanized to include a malicious payload in the form of a sideloaded DLL. This DLL is loaded at runtime by the legitimate application, collects system information, and beacons to attacker-controlled infrastructure, enabling remote command and control and potential delivery of additional malware. This constitutes a supply chain attack, as the legitimate application was modified to include and execute unauthorized code without user consent.

execution_context.file_location: 3CXDesktopApp installation directory, malicious DLL (e.g., ffmpeg.dll or d3dcompiler_47.dll) loaded by the main executable
required_permissions: filesystem (read/write for DLL loading and potential persistence)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At application launch, the code is loaded as a DLL by the main 3CXDesktopApp process, collects system information from the host, and sends this data via outbound HTTPS to an attacker-controlled domain, establishing a command and control channel.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes within the context of a trusted, signed application but performs unauthorized network communication to external, attacker-controlled domains and collects sensitive system information without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate VoIP application should not load non-standard DLLs or perform covert network beacons to untrusted infrastructure, nor should it exfiltrate system information outside of transparent, vendor-owned telemetry endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some applications may check for updates or send telemetry, but these actions are typically directed to official vendor domains, are documented, and do not involve sideloaded DLLs or covert data exfiltration.
key_indicators: DLL sideloading of non-standard or recently modified libraries (e.g., ffmpeg.dll, d3dcompiler_47.dll)
Outbound HTTPS requests to domains not associated with 3CX or its vendors
Execution of malicious code within the context of a signed, trusted application process
Collection and exfiltration of host system information at application startup

attack_chain.action: User downloads and installs the trojanized 3CXDesktopApp from the official or compromised distribution channel.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious DLL is present on the system.

attack_chain.action: Upon application launch, the malicious DLL (e.g., ffmpeg.dll or d3dcompiler_47.dll) is loaded by the main 3CXDesktopApp process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in the context of the trusted application.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code collects system information and beacons to attacker-controlled infrastructure via outbound HTTPS.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishes command and control, enabling further malicious activity such as additional payload delivery or data exfiltration.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected DLL loading by a signed application (e.g., 3CXDesktopApp loading ffmpeg.dll or d3dcompiler_47.dll not matching known-good hashes)
Network beacons to untrusted or newly registered domains at application startup from the 3CXDesktopApp process
Collection and exfiltration of system information by a VoIP or communications app outside of normal telemetry endpoints
file_indicators: Presence of non-standard or recently modified DLLs in the 3CXDesktopApp installation directory (e.g., ffmpeg.dll, d3dcompiler_47.dll) with hashes not matching official releases
Unexpected changes to application binaries or supporting libraries in the 3CXDesktopApp directory
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS requests from 3CXDesktopApp to attacker-controlled domains (domains not associated with 3CX, often newly registered or with no prior reputation)
Beaconing behavior (regular or periodic outbound connections) shortly after application launch
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor the 3CXDesktopApp process for loading of unexpected DLLs, especially ffmpeg.dll or d3dcompiler_47.dll with unknown or suspicious hashes. Inspect outbound network traffic from the application for connections to untrusted or newly registered domains. Alert on collection and exfiltration of system information by the application to non-vendor endpoints. Use EDR or AV solutions to detect known malicious variants of the trojanized DLLs and monitor for changes in the application directory.
